content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat chocolate milk (1 % fat) is a beverage made from skimmed cow’s milk, cocoa powder, and sweetener. It retains the creamy taste and nutritional profile of milk while providing far less fat than regular chocolate milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Low‑fat chocolate milk is popular in sports nutrition because it offers high protein with low calories.
Cocoa powder adds flavonoid antioxidants that may support cardiovascular health.
In many markets the drink is fortified with vitamin D and calcium to offset the loss of fat‑soluble nutrients.
Sugar levels are often reduced compared with full‑fat versions, but sweeteners are added to keep the chocolate flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A typical serving provides about 8 g of high‑quality milk protein, supporting muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: With roughly 50 kcal per 100 ml, it fits well into weight‑management plans.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Despite the low fat, the drink remains a good source of calcium for bone health, often fortified with vitamin D for better absorption.

items.title: Cocoa antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids in cocoa may reduce oxidative stress and improve vascular function.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Milk contains electrolytes such as potassium and sodium, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: As a dairy product, it can cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey should avoid this beverage.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some versions contain added sugars; those monitoring blood glucose should check the label.

items.title: Vitamin fortification
items.content: Excessive consumption of fortified drinks may lead to vitamin A or D overdose.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Low‑fat chocolate milk can be enjoyed as a refreshing drink, blended into smoothies, used as a base for protein shakes, or poured over oatmeal, pancakes, and cereal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as it may alter texture.
